label: conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge
title: Resurgent Stokes constants are Donaldson--Thomas / BPS degeneracies (the closed-sector state-integral bridge, GGM Conjecture 3(d) + GPPV)
html:
Conjecture (closed-sector state-integral bridge — Vol-conjecture-style adoption). For a hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the resurgent Stokes constant of the state integral of S^3 \setminus K on its distinguished (geometric Borel) ray is a Donaldson--Thomas invariant / BPS degeneracy of the associated 3d \mathcal{N}=2 theory T[K]:

  \mathfrak{S}(K) \;=\; \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) \;=\; \dim \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]),

where \mathfrak{S}(K) is the Stokes constant, \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) the Donaldson--Thomas / Kontsevich--Soibelman invariant of the q-difference structure, and \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]) the space of BPS states whose graded dimension categorifies the 3d index.

The first equality is [garoufalidis-gu-marino2023peacock] Conjecture 3(d) — "the Stokes constants are integers corresponding to the Donaldson--Thomas invariants and the BPS degeneracies" — which Garoufalidis--Gu--Mariño state as a conjecture and do not prove for any knot, 4_1 included. What they prove is their Conjecture 5 for 4_1 and 5_2 (their Theorem 6, via Theorems 17 and 25), and they verify Conjecture 4 for both knots by computation (§5.2, §6.2). The second is the [gukov-pei-putrov-vafa2017] (GPPV) realisation of the DT/BPS count as the graded dimension of the fivebrane BPS Hilbert space of T[M_3] on M_3 \times D^2, categorifying the 3d \mathcal{N}=2 indices. The 3d--3d dictionary itself --- the assignment of a 3d \mathcal{N}=2 theory T[M] to an ideally triangulated 3-manifold, with S^3 \setminus 4_1 worked explicitly, and the assembly of its S^3_b partition function (the state integral whose Stokes constants appear above) from tetrahedron factors --- is [dimofte-gaiotto2011] §4.1, §4.6 and §6.3. The 3d index of that theory is [dimofte-gaiotto-gukov2013] (DGG).

Part of the second equality is a theorem on a restricted class: [murakami-y2022] proves that for plumbed 3-manifolds with negative-definite linking matrix the Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant is the radial limit of the homological block \hat{Z}. That class consists of closed manifolds; S^3 \setminus K for a hyperbolic knot is cusped and not plumbed, so the result does not reach the objects this conjecture quantifies over, and the field dt_eq_bps below stays an assumption rather than a citation.

Which BPS sector — the non-degeneracy result

Two published knot-homology/BPS bridges live in the literature, and they identify different BPS spaces:

Bridge BPS sector 4_1 count
Gukov--Stošić [gukov-stosic2012] open BPS states (conormal L_K \subset T^*S^3; colored HOMFLY homology) \det(4_1) = 5
GPPV [gukov-pei-putrov-vafa2017] + GGM Conj 3(d) closed / state-integral (\hat{Z}; resurgent Stokes) 3

The closed-sector entry is the 4_1 Stokes integer of GGM eq. (60) (§3.1, the 4_1 knot when u = 0). The integer 4 that has been quoted beside it comes from GGM eqs. (96)/(98), which are 5_2 data (§3.2), not 4_1 data.

The open-HOMFLY count is fixed by the knots--quivers correspondence [kucharski-reineke-stosic-sulkowski2017]: the quiver of a knot has one node per HOMFLY-PT homology generator, so the 4_1 open-BPS count is \det(4_1) = 5.

That count is read off a published quiver, not inferred from the determinant. Singh et al. [singh-physrevd108106023] give the figure-eight explicitly, as a motivic sum over d_1 + \cdots + d_5 = r with a symmetric 5 \times 5 matrix C_{4_1}: five nodes, directly. The correspondence's rule --- node count equals determinant --- is itself confirmed at four knots rather than at one, so the identification is not a coincidence of the figure-eight:

knot published quiver \det
3_1 3 \times 3 (worked trefoil of [kucharski-reineke-stosic-sulkowski2017]) 3
4_1 5 \times 5 5
6_1 9 \times 9 9
8_1 13 \times 13 13

All four counts equal 1 + 4pm, the determinant of the double twist knot K(p, -m) implied by the Alexander polynomial of [singh-physrevd108106023]. Since 5 \neq 3, the open-HOMFLY Gukov--Stošić bridge does not reproduce the 4_1 Stokes integer 3 of GGM eq. (60) and does not license A_\omega = 3. Only the closed-sector bridge stated above relates to that integer; its q \to 0 anchor S^+(0)_{01} = 3 is machine-checked unconditionally (QOU.QBeta.StokesQZeroDTCount).

We therefore adopt the closed-sector bridge, and A_ω=3 is made conditional on it downstream (thm:aomega-fourone-dt-count) — conditional for every knot, 4_1 included, since GGM's Conjecture 3(d) is not proved for 4_1. It is not the open-HOMFLY bridge.

Lean axiomatisation

The bridge is a Lean typeclass QOU.QBeta.StokesDTBPSBridge carrying the two identifications as fields:

class StokesDTBPSBridge (Knot : Type*) where
  stokesConstant : Knot → ℤ
  dtInvariant    : Knot → ℤ
  bpsDim         : Knot → ℤ
  stokes_eq_dt : ∀ K, stokesConstant K = dtInvariant K   -- GGM Conj 3(d)
  dt_eq_bps    : ∀ K, dtInvariant K   = bpsDim K          -- GPPV

The fields are the conjecture's inputs; no field asserts a value of A_\omega. Any instance is the conjecture holding; none is supplied (the general statement is open for every knot, 4_1 included). Downstream results take [StokesDTBPSBridge Knot] as an explicit hypothesis and are then fully verified by Lean modulo that class instance, following the same pattern as conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture.
